title: Letter and Parish
premise: Hazel Thornbury, a night-shift dispatcher who has spent a decade making himself unnoticeable in the fading parish of Wrenlow, is pulled into a murder investigation when the victim—a retired solicitor—is found wearing clothes stolen from Hazel's own closet. The dead man had been quietly investigating a thirty-year-old inheritance fraud that rewrote who belonged to the parish's founding family, and Hazel's stolen clothes were meant to frame him as the killer. As Hazel closes cases no one else can, he uncovers that his own adoption was part of the original fraud, and that the murderer is the one person who has shown him loyalty all along. In the end, Hazel must choose between protecting the friend who killed to keep their shared secret buried and telling a truth that will finally give him a real place to belong.
about_author: Emrys Brightwater is the pen name of a former rural newsroom reporter who spent seven years covering small-town courts and estate disputes before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people who live at the edges of tight-knit communities, drawing on a childhood spent moving between foster homes in the English countryside.

chapters.title: The Night Shift
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. A routine Friday dispatching taxis through rain-soaked Wrenlow establishes Hazel's gift for noticing everything and being noticed by no one, and his careful distance from the parish's old families. When retired solicitor Ambrose Pell fails to arrive for his standing 2 a.m. taxi, Hazel feels the first wrong note. Emotional beat: quiet competence shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. Ambrose is found strangled in the churchyard, dressed in Hazel's own jacket and scarf, taken from his flat's communal laundry. Detective Inspector Sorrel Cade interviews Hazel, whose perfect memory of every fare makes him both witness and suspect. Emotional beat: the horror of visibility—the invisibility he cultivated becomes evidence against him.

chapters.title: The Solicitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. Searching Ambrose's office with taxi driver and reluctant ally Dev, Hazel finds a ledger of the 1995 Harrowgate inheritance case—notes suggesting the true heir was swapped and a birth record forged. Someone ransacked the office before them. Emotional beat: curiosity hardening into obsession; the past has teeth.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Hazel and DI Cade. Cade reconstructs the night of the murder while Hazel interviews elderly parishioners who each remember the Harrowgate scandal differently—and each has an alibi too neat by half. Emotional beat: mounting dread as every pillar of the parish community shows a crack.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Kept the Keys
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. Marigold Fenwick, the parish's aging postmistress and the only person who has always been kind to Hazel, reveals she witnessed the baby swap in 1995 but stayed silent out of love for the family. She warns Hazel to stop digging. Emotional beat: warmth laced with threat; kindness revealed as surveillance.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. Following the forged records, Hazel discovers his own adoption papers carry the same notary stamp as the fraudulent 1995 documents—he may be the swapped child himself, planted in the system to bury the true heir. Emotional beat: vertigo; the mystery turns inward and his sense of self fractures.

chapters.title: What Dev Knew
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. Hazel realizes Dev has been feeding his movements to someone, and confronts him; Dev confesses he was paid years ago to watch the orphaned boy, but swears he protected Hazel out of genuine loyalty. That same night, Marigold is found unconscious, her post office ransacked. Emotional beat: betrayal and tenderness tangled together.

chapters.title: The Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel and Cade. The trail leads to Edmund Harrowgate, the 'rightful' heir whose legitimacy depends on the fraud holding—but Edmund has an ironclad alibi for the murder, and Cade begins to believe the killer is protecting the secret rather than profiting from it. Emotional beat: the ground shifts; motive inverts.

chapters.title: Confession at the Crossing
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. Lured by a fake dispatch call to the old tollhouse where the swap happened, Hazel faces the killer: Marigold, conscious again and desperate, who killed Ambrose to keep her silence intact and framed Hazel because his questions endangered them both. She claims she did it all for Hazel—to keep him safe inside the lie. Emotional beat: climax; loyalty and truth collide at knife-point.

chapters.title: Letter and Parish
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. Marigold confesses publicly; the Harrowgate inheritance is unwound, and the true heir—an unassuming farmhand—chooses to share the estate rather than claim it alone. Hazel, offered his 'rightful' name, instead keeps Thornbury, but for the first time as a choice rather than a hiding place. Emotional beat: resolution; belonging earned through truth, not inherited through lies.
